channel.title: Avora Matcha Journal
channel.description: The Avora Matcha Journal. Everything about ceremonial-grade matcha: how to whisk it, where it comes from, its health benefits, and the story behind Avora. Sourced from Kyoto & Kagoshima, Japan.

item.title: Ceremonial vs. Culinary Matcha: What's the Difference?
item.description: Ceremonial-grade and culinary-grade matcha differ in harvest, leaf quality, color, taste, and price. Here is how to choose the right grade for drinking, lattes, and baking.

item.title: How to Choose a Matcha Brand (What Actually Matters)
item.description: Not sure which matcha to buy? A simple checklist for choosing a matcha brand: grade, harvest, origin, color, freshness, and price per serving.

item.title: How to Make Matcha: A Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners
item.description: A simple, foolproof method for making a smooth, frothy bowl of matcha at home: the tools you need, the right water temperature, ratios, and whisking technique.

item.title: How to Store Matcha So It Stays Fresh
item.description: Matcha is a fresh product that fades fast. Learn how to store matcha properly: away from air, light, heat, and moisture, so every bowl stays vibrant and smooth.

item.title: Is Avora Matcha Worth It? Cafe Matcha vs. Making It at Home
item.description: A cafe matcha latte in India costs around 400 rupees. A 30g tin of Avora is 1,199 rupees and makes about 15 bowls. Here is the honest cost breakdown.

item.title: 13 Fascinating Facts About Matcha
item.description: Where matcha comes from, why it is so green, how it is made, and what makes it different from every other tea. Thirteen genuinely interesting facts about ceremonial matcha.

item.title: Matcha Health Benefits: Energy Without the Crash
item.description: What makes matcha different from coffee: L-theanine, antioxidants (EGCG), and steady caffeine. A clear look at matcha health benefits and how to get them.

item.title: How to Make a Matcha Latte (Hot or Iced)
item.description: A simple matcha latte recipe you can make at home in five minutes. The right ratio of matcha, water, and milk for a smooth, cafe-quality latte, hot or iced.

item.title: Matcha vs. Coffee: Which Should You Drink?
item.description: Matcha and coffee both give you energy, but they feel completely different. A clear comparison of caffeine, focus, jitters, crash, and taste to help you choose.

item.title: Why Does My Matcha Taste Like Grass? (And How to Fix It)
item.description: If your matcha tastes bitter, grassy, or flat, the problem is usually one of five things: grade, freshness, water temperature, technique, or storage. Here is how to fix each.
